findings.expected: The WO states the rule that makes the ineligible outcome-flipping T3->5 fixture score 2/6, so markers can reproduce it and generalise to other outcome-flipping misreads.
findings.actual: WO:75 gives only the result: 'T3->5 earns canonical R2 and R5 only, 2/6'. The reason (R1 misses the printed-interval decision; R5 earned as an attempted primitive evaluated at two bounds) is only in the author script. R1 and R5 are both M marks whose only defect is using T=5. R1 is lost and R5 kept, but neither the WO nor the JSON explains why.
findings.evidence: My criterion-by-criterion score: R1 0 (no comparison with the printed (0,3)), R2 1, R3 0 (DM on R1), R4 0, R5 1 via WO:50 route 2 'signed sum of the legs from (a)', R6 0 = 2/6. So 2/6 follows the literal text. Defensible alternatives exist: (1) 4/6, under the Cambridge M note (9709_m16_ms_12 PDF2: 'Method marks are not lost for numerical errors') and the calculus ineligible fixtures (flat object-change keeps M I2/I5; implicit a3->4 keeps H1/N1/N2); (2) 1/6, if R5 route 1 'whole-interval' is read against [0,3] for a learner who writes F(5)-F(0) directly. Misread maths verified: 77/2 and 185/6.
findings.repair: Add one sentence to WO:75 (and the JSON eligibility note): an outcome-flipping datum voids the decision mark R1, because the roots were not compared with the printed interval, and so voids R3; R2 is independent of T; R5 is earned from the learner's own legs or a full-interval primitive evaluation, given benefit of the doubt. Alternatively, if Vitalis prefers the M-mark convention, re-mark to 4/6. Either way it remains an MR03-OPS proposal.

findings.expected: The separation disclosure states the highest single/pair accuracy found across all tested features, and does not imply that no simple rule separates the classes.
findings.actual: 'Best single/pair lookup is 156/168' covers only the 28 visible-feature tests. Codex's own derived pair (d/a, T) reaches 162/168 in the same file. Two simple derived rules also exist: the one-sided threshold |d| >= 2.5|a|T holds for 18/24 no-change cases and 0/144 sign-change cases (the same pattern as D3's |b| >= 4|a|), and fitted two-threshold rules separate all 168, e.g. 'no change iff -b/a >= T-1 or |d| >= 2.5|a|T'.
findings.evidence: motion/sep.py, sep2.py, onesided.py: 24/0 and 18/0 counts verified. Neither rule is learner-plausible without analysing v. Every perfect single feature I found evaluates v at T (sign(v(0)v(T)), v(T)/a) or recovers the roots from the coefficients (Vieta); both are legitimate analysis. Marks are protected because R1 requires a justified decision.
findings.repair: Qualify the headline as 'visible single/pair', cite (d/a,T) 162/168, and add one line: fitted rules on derived ratios can separate this finite bank, so the decision still has to be justified. No domain change is needed.

The same question arises for a same-outcome mixed T misread (R2 vs R4).
